title: Trading In Securities Policy

tiers.name: Meridian Persons
tiers.description: Directors and employees of, and contractors and secondees to, Meridian or any of Meridian's subsidiaries. Subject to the three general rules: no insider trading, no short term trading without General Counsel approval, and no transactions in Associated Products. No trading approval or blackout regime applies to this tier.

tiers.name: Meridian Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All directors of Meridian; the Chief Executive, all members of the Executive Management Team and their direct reports; all legal and investor relations staff; all staff who are members of the Long Term Incentive Plan; during a buyback, those involved in or with knowledge of it; and anyone else notified by the General Counsel. Subject to five additional rules: holdings disclosure, the Blackout Period ban, prior General Counsel approval for all trading, post-trade notification, and the margin loan prohibition. They remain deemed Meridian Restricted Persons for six months after departure.

tiers.name: all directors of Meridian
tiers.description: Distinguished for approval mechanics (the approval form must be countersigned by the Chair, or for the Chair by the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee) and for post-trade notification feeding the ASX Appendix 3Y and concurrent NZX lodgement.

tiers.name: the Chief Executive, all members of the Executive Management Team and their direct reports
tiers.description: Senior executive tier within Meridian Restricted Persons. The Chief Executive's approval form must be countersigned by the Chair or Deputy Chair; the Chief Executive and their direct reports also have NZ statutory relevant-interest disclosure obligations.

tiers.name: all staff who are members of the Long Term Incentive Plan
tiers.description: Plan membership alone makes a person a Meridian Restricted Person, so every LTI participant is inside the approval, blackout and margin loan regime as well as the Associated Products ban.

tiers.name: companies, trusts and other entities controlled by any Meridian Person and any family member or other person acting on the direction or recommendation of a Meridian Person
tiers.description: The Policy applies directly to these persons and entities, not merely by requiring the Meridian Person to procure their compliance. The margin loan ban is expressly extended to holdings in the name of spouses, partners or dependent children, trusts of which the person is trustee, and any company the person controls.

definitions.hedging_definition: An Associated Product is any product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any entitlement a Meridian Person is eligible for under the remuneration scheme.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Meridian's General Counsel may specify any other Blackout Period from time to time in relation to Meridian Securities, and any period in relation to specified Other Financial Products, either generally for all Meridian Restricted Persons or in relation to specified Meridian Restricted Persons. The General Counsel may also notify additional persons as Meridian Restricted Persons by name, designation, position or business group. The Policy does not say whether such periods or notifications are confidential.

rules.section: What this policy applies to; Additional Rules Two and Three
rules.detail: No express derivatives rule. 'Meridian Securities' expressly includes options or derivatives in respect of any securities of Meridian, and the exchange-traded qualifier attaches only to the residual limb 'any other financial product that is traded on a financial market', so an OTC put and call over Meridian shares is a Meridian Security. Trading in it therefore needs prior written General Counsel approval and is barred in Blackout Periods.
rules.evidence: any other securities of Meridian or its subsidiaries, including any debentures, convertible notes, units of shares, options or derivatives (including futures contracts listed on a futures exchange) in respect of any securities of Meridian or its subsidiaries and any other financial product that is traded on a financial market.

rules.section: Rules applicable to all Meridian Persons
rules.detail: Meridian Persons who are not Restricted Persons need no approval and are not subject to Blackout Periods; they are constrained only by the insider trading ban, the three-month short term trading rule and, if they participate in an equity-based remuneration scheme, the Associated Products ban.
rules.evidence: Meridian's trading in securities policy consists of: Three rules applicable to all Meridian Persons; Five additional rules applicable to Meridian Restricted Persons

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no approval route, on any product limiting the economic risk of participating in an entitlement under an equity-based remuneration scheme. It binds every Meridian Person entitled to participate in such a scheme, and so covers all LTI participants and all Restricted Persons who hold plan entitlements.
rules.evidence: Where Meridian Persons are entitled to participate in any equity-based remuneration scheme, they must not enter into any transaction for any 'Associated Product'. An Associated Product is any product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any entitlement a Meridian Person is eligible for under the remuneration scheme.

rules.detail: Rule Three is drafted around 'participating in any entitlement a Meridian Person is eligible for under the remuneration scheme' rather than around vesting, so shares that have vested but remain held under the scheme or subject to a restriction are still an entitlement under it and cannot be hedged. The Policy nowhere uses the language of vesting or holding locks.
rules.evidence: any product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any entitlement a Meridian Person is eligible for under the remuneration scheme

rules.detail: Once scheme shares have vested and been delivered free of restriction they arguably cease to be an 'entitlement a Meridian Person is eligible for under the remuneration scheme', taking them outside Rule Three; the same is true of shares bought on market. A collar over such shares is still a trade in Meridian Securities requiring prior written General Counsel approval, outside a Blackout Period. The boundary is untested on the face of the Policy.
rules.evidence: Before trading in Meridian Securities outside of a Blackout Period ... Meridian Restricted Persons must, using the form at the back of this policy: seek approval from the General Counsel

rules.detail: For a Meridian Person who is not a Restricted Person, hedging shares that are no longer an entitlement under a remuneration scheme is not prohibited and requires no approval, subject only to the insider trading ban.
rules.evidence: Where Meridian Persons are entitled to participate in any equity-based remuneration scheme, they must not enter into any transaction for any 'Associated Product'.

rules.section: Rule One ('Trade'); Additional Rules Three and Five
rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar is an agreement to dispose of Meridian Securities and so a trade needing General Counsel approval; if it is monetised by a loan secured on Meridian Securities it is separately caught by the Additional Rule Five ban, and if it monetises a scheme entitlement it is an Associated Product.
rules.evidence: 'Trade' includes applying for, acquiring or disposing of securities or other financial products, or agreeing to do so.

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy, and there is no speculative trading ban. A short sale would still be a disposal of Meridian Securities and so a trade requiring General Counsel approval for a Restricted Person.
Securities lending is not named and is not within the definition of 'Trade', which reaches only applying for, acquiring or disposing of securities or agreeing to do so.

rules.section: What this policy applies to; Additional Rule Three
rules.detail: CFDs are not named. A CFD over Meridian shares is a derivative in respect of securities of Meridian and so a Meridian Security, making it a trade requiring prior General Counsel approval; there is no speculative trading ban to bar it outright, but a CFD position opened and closed within three months would breach Rule Two.
rules.evidence: options or derivatives (including futures contracts listed on a futures exchange) in respect of any securities of Meridian or its subsidiaries

rules.detail: Outright ban with no approval route, expressly retrospective ('or continue with'), covering both loans to fund acquisition of Meridian Securities and loans in relation to which Meridian Securities may be used as security. Extended to holdings in the name of spouses, partners, dependent children, trusts where the person is trustee, and controlled companies.
rules.evidence: Meridian Restricted Persons may not enter into or continue with any margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Meridian Securities or in relation to which Meridian Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan.

rules.detail: Additional Rule Five binds only Meridian Restricted Persons; the Policy is silent on margin loans by other Meridian Persons.

Granting security over Meridian Securities is not itself a 'Trade', but the second limb of Additional Rule Five bans any arrangement 'in relation to which Meridian Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan'. The noun in the sentence is 'margin loan arrangements', so a purist could argue a bespoke bank facility is outside it, but the second limb and the stated rationale (forced sale in a Blackout Period) point the other way.
rules.evidence: any margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Meridian Securities or in relation to which Meridian Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan

rules.detail: No encumbrance or pledge rule applies to Meridian Persons outside the Restricted Person population, and granting security is not a 'Trade'.

The loan leg of a funded collar is a loan in relation to which Meridian Securities are used as security against repayment, which Additional Rule Five prohibits for every Restricted Person, including through a spouse, dependent child, trust or controlled company, with no approval, hardship or exceptional-circumstances route. The General Counsel's exceptional-circumstances discretion is expressed only in relation to Blackout Period trading, not Rule Five.
rules.evidence: This is because the terms of such a loan may require the sale of Meridian Securities during a Blackout Period or while the Meridian Restricted Person is in possession of inside information.

rules.detail: Secured financing is regulated only through Additional Rule Five, which applies to Meridian Restricted Persons alone.

Acquiring and then selling Meridian Securities within three months is banned for everyone, subject only to advance General Counsel approval in exceptional circumstances. There is no carve-out for shares acquired on vesting under an incentive plan.
rules.evidence: Meridian Persons must not engage in short term trading (i.e. acquiring and then selling Meridian Securities within a three month period), unless there are exceptional circumstances discussed and approved in advance by Meridian's General Counsel.

In those circumstances, the approval is automatically deemed to be withdrawn.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Meridian Restricted Persons may not enter into or continue with any margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Meridian Securities or in relation to which Meridian Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The second limb catches any loan secured on Meridian Securities, so the funded leg of a collar is prohibited for every director, executive and LTI participant, with no approval route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: may not enter into or continue with any margin loan arrangements
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban is not merely prospective, so an existing secured facility must be unwound rather than grandfathered, and a person becoming a Restricted Person must exit any such arrangement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This restriction applies whether the Meridian Securities are held: in the name of the Meridian Restricted Person; or in the name of their spouses or partners or dependent children; or by trusts of which the Meridian Restricted Person is a trustee; or by any company which a Meridian Restricted Person controls.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the secured borrowing through a family trust or controlled company does not escape the prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where Meridian Persons are entitled to participate in any equity-based remuneration scheme, they must not enter into any transaction for any 'Associated Product' ... any product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any entitlement a Meridian Person is eligible for under the remuneration scheme.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An absolute, approval-proof ban on the option legs to the extent they hedge scheme entitlements; it turns on eligibility under the scheme rather than on vesting, so the safest collar covers only shares acquired independently of any plan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Meridian Restricted Persons remain subject to this policy and will be deemed to be Meridian Restricted Persons for six months after their departure from Meridian.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A retiring director or executive cannot put on a funded collar for six months after leaving, so the bank must diligence departure dates rather than current office.

bespoke_clauses.topic: loan itself may be a security
bespoke_clauses.clause: Security is defined broadly and includes any interest in, or right to participate in, any capital, assets, earnings, royalties, or other property of any person, and any interest in, or right to be paid, money that is, or is to be deposited with, lent to, or otherwise owing by, any person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: On its face the definition sweeps in debt claims, so the loan and the OTC option confirmations could themselves be characterised as securities under the Policy, reinforcing that every leg needs General Counsel approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: must complete the approved trade within 10 trading days from the date of notification ... trading is still prohibited if a Meridian Restricted Person who has secured approval either has, or learns of, material information which is not generally available to the market. In those circumstances, the approval is automatically deemed to be withdrawn.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing and execution of the option legs must complete within 10 trading days (2 trading days if approved for a Blackout Period), and the approval evaporates automatically if material information arises before signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In the case of proposed trading by a director or the Chief Executive, the form must be signed by the Chair or, in the Chair's absence, the Deputy Chair and in the case of proposed trading by the Chair, the form must be signed by the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Board-level sign-off, not merely a General Counsel tick, is needed before a director or the Chief Executive can execute any leg, which lengthens the lead time inside the 10 trading day window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any other period that Meridian's General Counsel specifies from time to time in relation to Meridian Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unannounced blackouts can be imposed on all or specified Restricted Persons at any time, blocking entry, roll, unwind or physical settlement of the structure.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no incentive plan carve-out from short term rule
bespoke_clauses.clause: Meridian Persons must not engage in short term trading (i.e. acquiring and then selling Meridian Securities within a three month period).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most policies there is no exemption for selling shares received on vesting, so shares acquired within three months should not be delivered into a collar settlement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: It also applies to companies, trusts and other entities controlled by any Meridian Person and any family member or other person acting on the direction or recommendation of a Meridian Person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The counterparty to the collar cannot be a family trust or controlled entity used to sidestep the approval and margin loan rules, as those entities are themselves bound.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This is because the terms of such a loan may require the sale of Meridian Securities during a Blackout Period or while the Meridian Restricted Person is in possession of inside information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Meridian's objection is to lender-driven forced sales, so an unfunded collar with cash settlement and no security interest is the structure most likely to be approvable; the Policy contains no forced-sale carve-out.

summary: A funded collar is not available to any Meridian director, executive or LTI participant. Additional Rule Five bans Meridian Restricted Persons from entering into or continuing with any loan arrangement in relation to which Meridian Securities may be used as security against repayment, expressly extending to spouses, dependent children, trusts and controlled companies, and there is no approval, hardship or exceptional-circumstances route out of it; the General Counsel's discretion reaches only Blackout Period and short term trading. The option legs are separately constrained: an OTC put and call over Meridian shares is a Meridian Security, so a Restricted Person needs prior written General Counsel approval on the prescribed form (countersigned by the Chair for directors and the Chief Executive), executed within 10 trading days, outside the 31 May and 30 November Blackout Periods and any period the General Counsel specifies. Rule Three separately bans, with no approval route and for all Meridian Persons, any product limiting the economic risk of an entitlement under an equity-based remuneration scheme, so the collar could in no event be written over plan entitlements. At most an unfunded, unsecured, cash-settled collar over independently acquired shares held for more than three months might be approved, and even that binds a departing executive for six months after they leave.
